production.note: US model years. Start: GM's NAIAS release for the 1997 Corvette ("The tail section on the 1997 version is quite different from past Corvettes."). End: GM Media's 2004 specification table still lists the coupe and convertible with the LS1 (gm-2004-corvette-specs); the C6 replaced it for 2005. The 1999-2000 hardtop (fixed-roof coupe) and the 2001-2004 Z06 are separate cars.

body.note: GM Media 2004 table, one cell: "2-door hatchback coupe, convertible and hardtop; rear-drive, front-engine". The convertible was added for 1998. The 1999–2000 fixed-roof hardtop (same 345 hp LS1) is a coupe body and is covered by this record; the Z06 (from 2001) is a separate record.

aspiration.note: "LS1 Pushrod V8 with aluminum block and heads"; no forced induction (inferred).

transmission.note: GM 1999 table: "6-speed manual (coupe & hardtop) 4-speed 4L60-E automatic overdrive". GM 2004 table: Hydra-Matic 4L60-E "4-speed automatic" "std on coupe and convertible"; Tremec T56 (MM6) "6-speed manual" "opt on coupe and convertible" (gm-2004-corvette-specs).

powerHp.note: 1997-2000 rating (LS1). Quote (GM table, 1999 C5 Corvette column): "Horsepower" "345 @ 5600 RPM". GM's 1997 NAIAS release: "The new engine is a 5.7-liter LS1small-block, producing 345 hp and 350 lb.-ft. of torque" (gm-1997-corvette-naias); GM's 2000 release: "Capable of kicking out 345 horsepower" (gm-2000-corvette-release). From 2001 the LS1 was rated 350 hp: GM Media 2004 table "Horsepower (hp / kw @ rpm): 350 / 261 @ 5200" (gm-2004-corvette-specs). Each rating covers four of the eight model years, so the launch rating (345 hp) is used; the reference year is 1999, the first 345 hp year with a GM curb weight found.

weightLb.note: 1999 coupe. Quote (GM table, 1999 C5 Corvette column): "Curb Weight" "3245 lbs. (coupe)". GM gives one coupe figure, not split by transmission (the automatic was standard, the 6-speed manual optional). No GM curb weight for 1997 or 1998 was found: Corvette Action Center's own (unattributed) 1997 table gives "3,229 (auto.trans.)" and "3,218 (man.trans.)" (cac-1997-specs). GM Media's 2004 table gives the 350 hp coupe "3246 / 1458" (gm-2004-corvette-specs). Corvette Action Center's own 1998 table also gives "3,245 (Coupe)" but is unattributed, so it is not cited as a source. GM's figure is not split by transmission; on the C5 the automatic was standard and the 6-speed manual optional.
